headline: Same-shop growth stays strong, margins and profit slip
summary_short: Dutch Bros' Q1 FY2026 revenue rose to $464.4M (+30.8% y/y, +4.7% q/q) on 16.3% shop-count growth and 8.3% systemwide same-shop sales growth, while net income attributable to Dutch Bros fell to $16.1M (-24.7% q/q) as company-operated gross margin compressed 190bps y/y on higher coffee and new-food-program costs.
summary_long: Revenue grew 30.8% y/y and 4.7% q/q to $464.4M on 16.3% shop growth (1,177 total shops) and 8.3% systemwide same-shop sales growth. Company-operated gross margin fell 190bps y/y as coffee and new-food-program costs outweighed labor-cost leverage; franchising gross profit rose $3.2M on higher franchise sales. SG&A rose $14.3M y/y on headcount, performance pay, and donations. Net income attributable to Dutch Bros was $16.1M (diluted EPS $0.13), down 24.7% q/q for reasons the filing doesn't address, though up 4.8% y/y. Cash fell to $263.5M (-16.7% y/y) as capex rose to $57.0M on new-shop builds and the Clutch Coffee acquisition; long-term debt declined to $201.5M. No forward guidance was issued in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by continued unit expansion (1,177 systemwide shops, +16.3% y/y) and accelerating same-shop sales (+8.3% systemwide), while cost inflation and SG&A growth held profit growth well below revenue growth.
Revenue grew 30.8% y/y on 16.3% growth in total shop count and 8.3% systemwide same-shop sales growth, itself split between +3.2% ticket and +5.1% transactions growth.

Beverage, food and packaging costs rose 120bps of company-operated revenue on higher coffee costs and the new food program's higher input costs; occupancy costs rose 130bps on new-shop rent under build-to-suit leases.

Company-operated gross margin fell 190bps y/y as commodity, food-program, and occupancy cost increases outweighed a 120bps labor-cost improvement from sales leverage and pricing; franchising gross profit rose $3.2M on higher franchise-partner sales and royalties.

SG&A rose $14.3M y/y (about $6.0M more headcount/performance pay, $2.0M donations, $1.8M advertising, $1.4M professional fees), which combined with margin compression held operating-income growth to 10.4% y/y despite 30.8% revenue growth.

Net income attributable to Dutch Bros rose 4.8% y/y as revenue growth outpaced a higher effective tax rate (12.4% vs 6.1%, on a smaller stock-compensation tax benefit); the sequential q/q decline is not addressed in the filing, which discusses only y/y comparisons.
Diluted EPS was flat y/y at $0.13 because a 4.8% rise in net income was offset by a 4.8% rise in weighted-average diluted shares from equity issuances; the q/q decline is not addressed in the filing.
Operating cash flow rose primarily on higher net income from year-over-year sales growth and leverage of SG&A costs.
Capex rose 25.1% y/y on new company-operated shop openings and the Clutch Coffee asset acquisition.
